# wasm-html-to-image

> High-performance WebAssembly HTML-to-image renderer and image optimization engine.
> Consolidates HTML rendering (Satoru / Skia / litehtml) and native image encoding (WebP / AVIF / JPEG) into a single, unified WASM binary.

## Core Capabilities
- **HTML to Image**: Render HTML strings, arrays (multi-page PDF), or remote URLs directly to PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, RAW, ThumbHash, SVG, or vector PDF.
- **Image Optimization & Conversion**: Direct image-to-image resizing, cropping, and format re-encoding (e.g., JPEG to WebP/AVIF, GIF to animated WebP) without HTML layout overhead.
- **Universal Runtime**: Runs seamlessly on Node.js (>=20), Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge Runtime, Browsers, Deno, and CLI.
- **Zero Heavy Dependencies**: NO Puppeteer, Chromium, Playwright, or node-canvas required.

---

## Installation

```bash
npm install wasm-html-to-image
```

---

## Subpaths & Environment Guide

Choose the appropriate import based on runtime and use case:

| Subpath | Target Environment | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `wasm-html-to-image` | Universal (Recommended) | Auto-routes: uses `workerd` on Cloudflare, `single` elsewhere. Direct `render()`. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/single` | Node.js, Bundlers | Self-contained single-bundle WASM entry with instant `render()`. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/workerd` | Cloudflare Workers | Pre-compiled `WebAssembly.Module` compatible with strict Cloudflare isolates. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/edge-light` | Vercel Edge Runtime | Tailored for edge sandbox memory and execution constraints. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/workers` | Node.js, Browsers (on workerd: no pool, falls back to direct execution) | Multi-threaded worker pool for high-throughput batch rendering. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/react` | React (JSX) | Directly render React element trees. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/preact` | Preact (JSX) | Directly render Preact element trees. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/tailwind` | Tailwind CSS | Inlines UnoCSS / Tailwind utility classes into inline CSS styles. |
| `wasm-html-to-image/index` | High-throughput servers | Manual WASM module reuse via `loadHtmlToImageModule()` and `htmlToImage()`. |

---

## Standard Usage Patterns

### 1. Zero-Config HTML Rendering

```typescript
import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image";

const result = await render({
  value: `<div style="padding: 20px; background: #1e293b; color: white; font-family: sans-serif;">
    <h1 style="margin: 0; font-size: 24px;">Hello World</h1>
  </div>`,
  width: 800,
  format: "png", // 'png' | 'jpeg' | 'webp' | 'avif' | 'jxl' | 'svg' | 'pdf' | 'raw' | 'thumbhash'
});

console.log(result.data); // Uint8Array (or string for format: 'svg')
console.log(result.width, result.height); // Output dimensions
```

### 2. Image Optimization & Format Conversion

Pass an image buffer (`Uint8Array` or `Buffer`) or a `data:image/...` URL directly to `render()`. The library automatically detects image magic bytes and skips the HTML layout pass.

```typescript
import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image";

const inputBuffer = await fs.readFile("input.jpg");

// Convert & compress JPEG -> WebP
const webp = await render({
  value: inputBuffer,
  width: 600, // Optional resize
  format: "webp",
  quality: 80, // 0-100
});

// Convert -> AVIF with speed control
const avif = await render({
  value: inputBuffer,
  width: 800,
  format: "avif",
  quality: 75,
  speed: 6, // 0 (best quality) - 10 (fastest)
});

// Crop and resize
const cropped = await render({
  value: inputBuffer,
  crop: { x: 50, y: 50, width: 300, height: 300 },
  width: 150,
  height: 150,
  format: "png",
});
```

### 3. Cloudflare Workers (root import recommended)

```typescript
// wrangler.jsonc: no "rules" needed on current Wrangler (v3/v4) —
// `import ... from "*.wasm"` is bundled as WebAssembly.Module by default.
// Minimal wrangler.jsonc: { "main": "src/index.ts", "compatibility_date": "2026-09-01" }
// (Only configure "rules" yourself if you customize bundling rules or use a very old Wrangler.
// Note: @cloudflare/vite-plugin ignores "rules".)

import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image"; // auto-selects the workerd build on Cloudflare ("wasm-html-to-image/workerd" also works)

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    const result = await render({
      value: `<h1 style="color: blue;">Edge OGP Image</h1>`,
      width: 1200,
      height: 630,
      format: "png",
    });

    return new Response(result.data, {
      headers: { "Content-Type": "image/png" },
    });
  },
};
```

### 4. Vercel Edge Runtime (`edge-light`: caller-supplied wasm required)

Unlike `workerd`, `edge-light` bundles no default wasm: `render(options, wasm)` requires a pre-compiled `WebAssembly.Module` as the 2nd argument.

```typescript
import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/edge-light";

const wasm = await WebAssembly.compile(
  await (await fetch(wasmUrl)).arrayBuffer(),
);

const result = await render(
  {
    value: `<h1 style="color: blue;">Edge OGP Image</h1>`,
    width: 1200,
    height: 630,
    format: "png",
  },
  wasm,
);
```

### 5. High-Throughput Worker Pool (`workers`)

```typescript
import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/workers";

const tasks = items.map((item) =>
  render({
    value: `<h1>${item.title}</h1>`,
    width: 600,
    height: 400,
    format: "webp",
  }),
);

const images = await Promise.all(tasks);
```

### 6. High-Throughput Server Module Reuse (`index`)

```typescript
import { loadHtmlToImageModule, htmlToImage } from "wasm-html-to-image/index";

// Load WASM module once at server boot
const mod = await loadHtmlToImageModule();

// Reuse in request handlers
app.get("/ogp", async (req, res) => {
  const result = await htmlToImage(mod, {
    value: `<h1>${req.query.title}</h1>`,
    width: 1200,
    height: 630,
    format: "png",
  });
  res.type("image/png").send(Buffer.from(result.data));
});
```

---

## Options Reference (`RenderOptions`)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string \| string[] \| Uint8Array \| ArrayBuffer` | - | HTML string, array of HTML strings (multi-page PDF), or raw image bytes (`Buffer` works as `Uint8Array`) |
| `url` | `string` | - | Remote URL to fetch and render (alternative to `value`) |
| `width` | `number` | `800` | Target viewport / output width in pixels |
| `height` | `number` | auto / content | Target viewport / output height in pixels |
| `format` | `string` | `"png"` | Output format: `"png"`, `"jpeg"`, `"webp"`, `"avif"`, `"jxl"`, `"svg"`, `"pdf"`, `"raw"`, `"thumbhash"`, `"none"` |
| `quality` | `number` | `85` | Compression quality (0-100) for JPEG, WebP, and AVIF |
| `speed` | `number` | `6` | CPU effort/speed (0=best quality/slowest, 10=fastest) for AVIF |
| `scale` | `number` | `1.0` | Device pixel ratio / render scaling factor |
| `crop` | `{ x, y, width, height }` | - | Rectangular cropping coordinates |
| `fallbackFonts` | `(Uint8Array \| Buffer)[]` | - | Inlined custom font binaries for air-gapped / offline rendering |
| `fonts` | `Record<string, Uint8Array \| Buffer>` | - | Font family mapping dictionary |
| `timeout` | `number` | `10000` | Timeout in milliseconds for resource loading |

Additional extension keys exist (e.g. `baseUrl`, `fit`, `animation`); see the type definitions for the full list.

---

## Critical Rules for AI Agents (Anti-Patterns to AVOID)

1. **NEVER use Puppeteer, Playwright, or Chromium with this package**: `wasm-html-to-image` compiles litehtml and Skia directly to WebAssembly. It operates entirely in-memory without browser processes.
2. **DO NOT install `@napi-rs/canvas` or `node-canvas`**: Canvas rendering is built directly into the unified WASM engine.
3. **DO NOT pass Base64 data back and forth unnecessarily**: Pass raw `Uint8Array` or `Buffer` directly to `render()`.
4. **Cloudflare Workers preference**: Import from `wasm-html-to-image` (recommended; auto-selects the workerd build on Cloudflare, explicit `wasm-html-to-image/workerd` also works) (no wrangler rules needed on current Wrangler; only needed if you customize bundling rules or use very old Wrangler).
5. **Google Fonts resolution**: Google Fonts are downloaded automatically in WOFF2 format by default. You do NOT need manual font download logic unless working offline.
